props.name: Half-cell findings rarely transfer to full electrolysers

evidence.quote: However, these half-cell setups suffer from low reactant mass transport, as reflected by unrealistic current densities and potential ranges, which are significantly different from those of full electrolyser systems. Consequently, findings obtained from catalyst- structure performance relationships in half cells can only rarely be transferred to full electrolysers.

Most of this research is performed using half-cell configurations, e.g. rotating disc electrodes, with the catalyst immersed completely in electrolyte without PTE to enhance gas–liquid mass transfer and contact.

props.scope: low-temperature water and CO2 electrolysis
props.statement: Findings from catalyst-structure-performance relationships obtained in half-cell setups (e.g. rotating disc electrodes) can only rarely be transferred to full electrolyser systems, because these setups suffer from low reactant mass transport and show unrealistic current densities and potential ranges.

props.name: More measurements with scalable tailor-made PTEs needed

evidence.quote: For experiments additional to investigations with backing electrodes bearing thin catalyst layers and aiming to determine the intrinsic catalyst properties, more and improved measurements with scalable and tailor-made PTEs should be conducted. Only with these PTEs, either in half-cell or full-cell arrangement, will the full complexity of the activity transport nexus be captured.

props.scope: experiments on water and CO2 electrolysis
props.statement: Beyond investigations with backing electrodes bearing thin catalyst layers, more and improved measurements with scalable and tailor-made PTEs (in half-cell or full-cell arrangement) should be conducted to capture the full complexity of the activity transport nexus.

props.name: Ionomer film controls local active-site concentrations with solid electrolytes

evidence.quote: The ionomer film controls the local concentrations at the active site (pH, CO2, products) and can be tuned accordingly

However, the role of the ionomer gains considerable importance with solid electrolytes, since a continuous ionomer film is necessary to transport the ions towards or away from the membrane to close the electric circuit.

props.scope: CO2 and water electrolysis with solid electrolytes
props.statement: With solid electrolytes the role of the ionomer gains considerable importance: a continuous ionomer film is necessary to transport ions towards or away from the membrane to close the electric circuit, and it controls the local concentrations at the active site (pH, CO2, products) and can be tuned accordingly.

props.name: Activities and selectivities differ between PTE and disk electrodes

evidence.quote: Mass transport limitations inside PTEs can provoke significant concentration and pH profiles, with mostly unknown conditions at the electrocatalyst. Thus, measured activities and selectivities of the same electrocatalyst can be different inside a PTE and on disk or carbon cloth/paper electrodes. This effect is particularly pronounced in CO2 electrolysis using liquid electrolytes at high current densities

props.note: The review cites this effect from [67]; it is not a run of this source.
props.scope: CO2 electrolysis with liquid electrolytes at high current densities
props.statement: Mass transport limitations inside PTEs can provoke significant concentration and pH profiles with mostly unknown conditions at the electrocatalyst, so measured activities and selectivities of the same electrocatalyst can differ between a PTE and disk or carbon cloth/paper electrodes, particularly in CO2 electrolysis with liquid electrolytes at high current densities.

props.name: Cell components and graded PTEs govern activity, selectivity, stability

evidence.quote: the structure and composition of these components can strongly influ­ence the activity, selectivity, and stability of the electrolysis system

PTEs enabling high current densities are graded hierarchical materials systems, containing large pore structures in the micrometer range for fast transport and small pores up to the single digit nanometer range in the catalyst layer.

props.scope: porous transport and catalyst layers of water and CO2 electrolysis cells
props.statement: The structure and composition of the cell components strongly influence the activity, selectivity and stability of the electrolysis system; PTEs enabling high current densities are graded hierarchical materials systems with large micrometre pores for fast transport and small pores down to the single-digit nanometre range in the catalyst layer.

props.name: CO2 depletion shifts CO2RR selectivity towards HER

evidence.quote: Depletion of CO2 leads to lower density of adsorbed CO species and thus fewer C–C coupled products, which consequently increases unwanted HER
In contrast to water electrolysis, selectivity can be largely influenced by species transport in CO2 reduction.

props.scope: CO2 electrolysis
props.statement: In CO2 reduction, depletion of CO2 lowers the density of adsorbed CO species and thus the formation of C-C coupled products, while increasing the unwanted hydrogen evolution reaction; selectivity can therefore be largely influenced by species transport.

props.name: PTEs central to high-performance CO2 electrolysis; interface poorly understood

evidence.quote: PTEs are clearly central to high performance CO2 electrolysis systems and their optimum transport and optimum interface properties must be better understood

Despite the importance of activity and selectivity, the precise impact of the form of the interface between gas and electrolyte phase and of the PTE is not yet clearly understood. So far, this interface is defined simply by a manufacturing approach resulting in a stochastic structure.

props.scope: CO2 electrolysis
props.statement: PTEs are central to high-performance CO2 electrolysis systems, but the precise impact of the form of the gas/electrolyte interface and of the PTE on activity and selectivity is not yet clearly understood; so far the interface is defined by a manufacturing approach resulting in a stochastic structure.

props.name: CO2 solubility limits non-PTE electrodes; PTEs reach above 1 A/cm2

evidence.quote: In CO2 electrolysis, non-PTE electrodes suffer from a limiting current density of a few mA/cm2 because the solubility of CO2 in the aqueous electrolyte is limited to ~ 33 mmol/l (at 298 K and 1 atm) and the thickness of the mass-transfer boundary layer over the electrode is typically of the order of 50 μm, even when vigorously stirring or recirculating the electrolyte
under 60 atm of CO2 a maximum partial current density towards formate of 560 mA/cm2 was reached
Partial current densities of CO2RR of more than 1 A/cm2 have been reached with liquid electrolytes

props.note: The quantitative values are this review's citations of other works (solubility and boundary layer from [67]; 560 mA/cm2 towards formate under 60 atm CO2 from Todoroki et al. [70]; more than 1 A/cm2 from [42,71]); they are not runs of this source.
props.scope: CO2 electrolysis in aqueous electrolytes
props.statement: Non-PTE CO2 electrolysis electrodes suffer from a limiting current density of a few mA/cm2 because the solubility of CO2 in aqueous electrolyte is limited (about 33 mmol/l at 298 K and 1 atm) and the mass-transfer boundary layer is of the order of 50 micrometres even when vigorously stirring or recirculating the electrolyte; pressurizing the electrolyte to 60 atm CO2 raised the maximum partial current density towards formate to 560 mA/cm2, and PTE electrodes reached CO2RR partial current densities of more than 1 A/cm2 with liquid electrolytes.

props.name: Only full flow cells address technical current density and crossover

evidence.quote: Only in this realistic arrangement can questions such as cell voltage at technically relevant current densities (typically at least 200 mA/cm2) and product crossover between the cathodic and anodic half-cell be properly addressed
When it comes to application-oriented measurements, full flow-cells with PTE electrodes are imperative because they are scalable in size and number (stacking).

props.scope: application-oriented measurements on water and CO2 electrolysers
props.statement: Only in full flow cells with PTE electrodes, which are scalable in size and number, can questions such as cell voltage at technically relevant current densities (typically at least 200 mA/cm2) and product crossover between the cathodic and anodic half-cell be properly addressed.

props.name: Bubble artefacts can mimic OER catalyst degradation

evidence.quote: in water electrolysis, nano- and micro-bubbles formed within the pores of the catalyst layer during the OER on disk or carbon cloth/paper electrodes cannot be removed and the corresponding potential increase can be mistakenly interpreted as catalyst degradation
Backing electrode degradation can occur under OER conditions and has to be either excluded or considered to accurately measure the electrocatalyst’s stability.

props.scope: OER stability testing on disk or carbon cloth/paper electrodes
props.statement: In water electrolysis, nano- and micro-bubbles formed within the pores of the catalyst layer during the OER on disk or carbon cloth/paper electrodes cannot be removed, and the corresponding potential increase can be mistakenly interpreted as catalyst degradation; backing-electrode degradation must be excluded or considered to measure the electrocatalyst stability accurately.

props.name: Flat vs porous electrode conditions differ; test at relevant conditions

evidence.quote: A simplified model comparing an H-cell and a gas-diffusion layer clearly demonstrates that conditions are very different between flat and porous electrodes (Fig. 7), and that catalyst performance must be assessed under more technically relevant conditions, such as that found in porous transport electrodes

props.note: The figure and the finding are reprinted from [67]; not a run of this source.
props.scope: CO2 reduction on gas-diffusion vs flat electrodes
props.statement: Model-based predictions show that conditions differ strongly between flat and porous electrodes, so catalyst performance must be assessed under more technically relevant conditions such as those found in porous transport electrodes (Fig. 7, reprinted from Burdyny & Smith [67]).

props.name: Multidisciplinary approach required for the activity transport nexus

evidence.quote: Any new research focus on the activity transport nexus should not draw research down to a purely technical scale
A multidisciplinary scientific approach is required and the following steps can pave the way towards realization:
Research communities need to interact more. During definition of research questions within the fields of natural, materials, and engineering sciences, strong and vivid interaction shall be sought.

props.scope: water and CO2 electrolysis research
props.statement: Research on the activity transport nexus should not be reduced to the purely technical scale; a multidisciplinary scientific approach across natural, materials and engineering sciences is required.

props.name: Tailored structured PTEs could reach the optimum PTE form

evidence.quote: The optimum form of PTEs for a specific reaction could be reached by structured materials specifically tailored for this purpose, e.g. made of linear pores, well-defined hierarchical structures, or PTEs with predefined liquid and gas pathways.

props.scope: porous transport electrodes for CO2 and water electrolysers (section 3.4 outlook)
props.statement: The optimum form of porous transport electrode for a specific reaction could be reached by structured materials specifically tailored for that purpose, e.g. made of linear pores, well-defined hierarchical structures, or PTEs with predefined liquid and gas pathways.
